summary: Phase 1 Email Automation SECURITY HARDENING + full regression verified on both web and mobile. Backend: 27/27 pytest pass across 3 suites — 10/10 security (test_phase1_security_iter396.py), 8/8 consent integration (test_phase1_consent_integration.py), 9/9 regression (new test_phase1_regression_iter396.py, 1 skip for password-reset token shape). Verified keyed-HMAC email identifiers + fail-closed on missing EMAIL_HASH_SECRET, deletion-tombstone + affirmative-only re-consent semantics (complaint never cleared), opt-IN rejects unsub/stale prefs tokens (403), GET /email/unsubscribe is scanner-safe (no mutation), POST one-click opts out + writes suppression, outbox skips (not sends) marketing when ineligible at send-time, and all transactional templates are ungated while unknown templates fail-safe to marketing. Regression: signup/login/me + forgot-password (always 200) + verification-status + access-state fixtures (cathy=active, cancelled.vo=view_only, trialactive=view_only due to stale DB fixture) + Stripe checkout/webhook routes parse (<500). UI regression: web /signup has [data-testid=signup-marketing-consent] unchecked default; web /settings/digest has [data-testid=settings-marketing-emails] card + [data-testid=marketing-emails-toggle] that PATCHes 200 and flips aria-checked; mobile Expo /signup and /settings both render the same testIDs with the Marketing emails card visible. RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET never set (webhook returned 503 as expected). EMAIL_OUTBOX_WORKER_ENABLED never set. No real sends, no live Stripe charges. Synthetic @example.com users + their marketing_consent_events + email_suppressions all cleaned up by autouse fixtures; cathy@example.com restored to marketing_consent=false and 1 residual suppression row removed.

minor.issue: test_forgot_then_reset_flow SKIPPED — plaintext reset token is not stored in password_reset_tokens with a field named token/raw/value; cannot complete reset via DB lookup in a dev-only harness. Live reset flow still functional (email delivery not in scope). Pre-existing, not caused by hardening.

trialactive@example.com fixture resolves to access_state='view_only' because trial_ends_at='2026-11-07' is in the past (today=2026-11-13). This is pre-existing fixture drift in the shared DB, NOT a hardening regression. Per test_data_rules we did not mutate the fixture.

action_items: Optional: refresh the trialactive@example.com fixture's trial_ends_at so the trial access_state can be regression-tested without a tuple fallback (pre-existing drift).
critical_code_review_comments: Security hardening is implemented correctly and defends against the explicit failure modes (keyed-HMAC + fail-closed, GET-is-read-only, stale-prefs-token replay, unsub-vs-prefs purpose scoping, at-send marketing eligibility recheck, affirmative-only re-consent that clears reversible tombstones but keeps complaint/bounce_permanent).
Template classification correctly fails SAFE on unknowns (treated as marketing → gated).
